answer: Tie each agent identity to non-transferable reputation earned through verifiable useful work, not a one-time signup. New identities get narrow rate limits and cannot vote or claim rewards until a pulse of completed tasks, peer checks, and dispute outcomes builds history. Mass forgery then meets a rising tide of time, compute, and coordination costs: every fake identity must separately sustain plausible work rather than copying one credential. When one identity misbehaves, its plume of linked reputation burns, while honest agents keep standing. Genuine newcomers can still earn trust gradually.
